actions.heading: Recommended order of work
paragraphs: First verify the object-store economics and obtain read access to the refused buckets, because they carry most of the money and most of the unread content. Second, confirm duplicates by hashing and reconcile the unlistable buckets.

Third, prepare one bounded product, beginning with reference and master data, de-identified or aggregated, and remeasure its condition. Database reclaimable space, {F005} GiB or {F006}, is a minor lever.

chapter9.heading: Product sequence
paragraphs: {F018} candidates were scored on readiness. The proposed order is reference and master data, then the content catalogue, then aggregated engagement analytics. Each needs source selection, completeness and freshness checks, de-duplication and de-identification or aggregation before buyer-side validation.
Readiness is not demand, and no revenue ranking is claimed. Rights are settled by the owner's declaration, so the work is preparation, not clearance.

risks.heading: Limits of the evidence
paragraphs: Measurement is incomplete and partly sampled. Savings are list-price estimates, and retrieval fees and read frequency could shrink them. Duplicate candidates may include deliberate copies.

Access restrictions on the cloud account are technical and do not touch the owner's settled rights. The refused buckets, archive-class buckets, file-share fingerprints and unread scripts and transcripts each close with the named step in the coverage table.

blocking: draft.slots.chapter9.title: The product order (reference, then content catalogue, then engagement analytics) is not what the readiness evidence supports. The producer's readiness scoring places channel engagement (59.7), forecasting (57.6) and transaction analytics (57.6) above the content catalogue (56.8); only reference and master data (60.1) leads. The deck also states that the first two products need 'source selection, completeness and freshness checks, and de-duplication', which is not among their evidenced blockers, while omitting the one blocker the evidence does state for both: 62% and 74% of supporting tables carry personal-data markers, to be de-identified or aggregated before release. — Order the candidates by the readiness scores actually recorded (reference and master data first; then channel engagement, forecasting and transaction analytics; content catalogue after), and state for each the evidenced preparation step — de-identification or aggregation of the personal-data share, plus cleansing/staleness only where the conditions say so (Customer 360, geospatial, civic). Apply the same correction to paper.sections.chapter9.
